# Copilot instructions — comic-vault-box-manager

Purpose: provide targeted, repo-specific guidance so future Copilot sessions understand how to build, run, and reason about this project quickly.

---

## 1) Build, run, test, and lint (commands)

- Install deps: npm install
- Dev (client + server with Vite middleware): npm run dev
- Build (client + bundle server): npm run build
- Start production bundle: npm run start
- Import collection from CSV: npm run import:collection
- Clean build artifacts: npm run clean
- Lint / type-check: npm run lint (runs `tsc --noEmit`)

Notes:
- There are no automated tests or test runner configured in this repo. No single-test command exists. Add a test framework (Vitest/Jest) if tests are needed.

---

## 2) High-level architecture (big picture)

- Full-stack TypeScript app:
  - server.ts: Express-based backend that exposes REST endpoints under /api/* and provides Vite middleware in development.
  - client: React + Vite in `src/` (entry: src/main.tsx, top-level App component in src/App.tsx).
  - Database: PostgreSQL is the system of record. On first successful connection the app migrates the browser-cached collection into PostgreSQL.

- Key integrations:
  - Gemini AI (Google GenAI) for cover-image scanning (requires GEMINI_API_KEY).
  - Google Drive + Google Sheets for import and cover selection (see services/driveService and Google Sheets fallback logic in server.ts).
  - PostgreSQL via `pg` pool; DDL generation and SQL export endpoints provided by the server.

- Build details:
  - `npm run build` runs Vite build for the client and uses esbuild to bundle `server.ts` into `dist/server.cjs`.
  - Dev mode uses Vite in middlewareMode so the Express server proxies and serves client assets during development.

---

## 3) Key conventions and repository-specific patterns

- Environment precedence: .env.local overrides .env. Put secrets (DATABASE_URL, GEMINI_API_KEY) in .env.local when developing.
- Local browser storage keys: `comic_vault_comics` and `comic_vault_boxes`. The app uses them as a local cache and migrates them into PostgreSQL on first DB run.
- Image handling: cover images may be large data-URIs. The client compresses/sets `NoImage.png` for very large images before sending to the server (see src/services/postgresService.prepareComic and utils/imageUtils).
- API surface (server):
  - GET /api/collection
  - PUT /api/comics/:id and PUT /api/comics (replace entire set)
  - DELETE /api/comics/:id
  - PUT /api/boxes/:id and PUT /api/boxes
  - DELETE /api/boxes/:id
  - POST /api/scan-cover (Gemini image analysis)
  - POST /api/google-sheets/fetch (Google Sheets import)
  - POST /api/export-sql (DDL + seed SQL generator)

- Database-safe upserts: server uses `ON CONFLICT` and transaction patterns when replacing entire collections/boxes—be careful to preserve that behavior when editing server code.
- Types: top-level `src/types.ts` centralizes domain interfaces (ComicBook, StorageBox). Prefer updating types there when changing domain shape.
- SQL schema: canonical schema is generated by `/api/export-sql` and initial migrations are in `db/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql`.

---

## 4) Where to look for common tasks

- Add a new API route: server.ts (it's single-file; keep server logic cohesive).
- Client UI changes: src/components/* — follow existing component split (Catalog, BoxManager, Modals).
- Data access patterns: src/services/postgresService.ts (client-side HTTP wrappers) and server.ts (actual DB queries).
- Image/CSV parsing utilities: src/utils/* (titleParser, imageUtils, dateUtils, boxUtils).

---

## 5) Environment variables (important ones)

- DATABASE_URL — required for PostgreSQL; if missing, the server returns 503 for DB routes.
- DATABASE_SSL — set to 'true' to use ssl with rejectUnauthorized: false.
- PORT — server listen port (default 3000).
- GEMINI_API_KEY — required for /api/scan-cover (Gemini AI).

---

## 6) Commit & PR guidance for Copilot sessions

- When changing database queries or schema, update `db/migrations/001_initial_schema.sql` (or create a new migration) and ensure export-sql still generates accurate DDL for both sqlite/postgres paths.
- Keep server-side SQL generation and client-side JSON shape (src/types.ts) in sync.

---

## 7) Playwright E2E tests (local & CI)

Local run (developer machine):
- Install: npm i -D @playwright/test
- Install browsers: npx playwright install
- Start the app server pointing at your local Postgres (example, replace PASSWORD):
  - PowerShell:
    $env:DATABASE_URL = 'postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@localhost:3001/comic_vault'; $env:PORT = '3000'; npm run dev
  - macOS / Linux (bash):
    DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:PASSWORD@localhost:3001/comic_vault' PORT=3000 npm run dev
- Run a single test:
  npx playwright test e2e/example.spec.ts
- Run test suite:
  npx playwright test

CI (GitHub Actions):
- Workflow provisions a temporary Postgres service (see .github/workflows/playwright.yml). The CI sets DATABASE_URL to a local service instance; no repo secrets are required for CI.
- If tests require seeded data, add a step to the workflow to apply migrations or import sample data before starting the server.
